evidence: Quint. 1.5.62: genetīvō cāsū nōn e litterā, sed tis syllabā terminārentur (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Short for cāsus genetīvus, the case of origin; Varro calls it patricius cāsus (Lewis & Short). Lewis & Short heads it genetīvus (“not genitīvus”, after Lachmann); Traupman writes genitīvus.

phrases.english: In what case is it? — The genitive.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 222, p. 246.
Quintilian checked against the Perseus Latin texts, and cited by its numbering.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 320.
